One concrete P2 gap: new partial parity slabs/propagation cannot sample derived scattered fields.

PortWave._combined at framework_waves.py:439 converts parity coefficients to helicity, which requires both polarization ports. Consequently, a newly supported one-port parity slab’s .scatter(negative=[1.]).positive.hfield(...) raises “polarization conversion requires both polarizations.” D/B/G/F fail through the same path. NumPy handles these fields without requiring complete pairs. Current partial-parity tests exercise power and propagation arrays only.

No concrete regression found in the axial polarization correction, D/B constitutive algebra, or conversion of complete internal polarization blocks before final projection. Read-only inspection; no execution or edits.

The strongest source-level explanation for the flat scatter/cylinder penalty is an unnecessary worker-pool handoff.

Candidate Evidence Smallest coherent fix
Single-column plane expansions enter the pool Both benchmarks pass one active helicity. pw/expand.rs:327 now unconditionally calls threads::install, including at a one-thread budget. Reuse try_fill_chunks with parallel = vectors.len() > 1. Preserve the existing computation and validation.
Repeated material validation PlaneWave.kvecs validates the same immutable material on every scatter/cross-width call. If still consequential, validate once in PlaneWave.__init__; retain checks for APIs accepting new materials and dynamic framework guards.
Identity polarization conversions allocate labels Framework slabs call change_port_polarization, which constructs PlaneWavePorts before discovering source and target match. Return immediately when source == target.

No new internal solve was added to the NumPy sphere-scatter or cylinder-width paths. Their output construction and cross-section calculations are unchanged. Preserve complete internal slab polarizations and final projection.

These are source-supported candidates, not measured attribution. Findings sent to root and correctness; no builds, tests or edits.

No concrete numerical-conclusion misstatement found in the inspected original Linux comparison.

  • All ten Linux suite manifests record 7421ca9 (now 5d7e06f) and matching native, Python and numerical hashes. This supports the original Linux campaign’s “same numerical code” claim.
  • The corrected campaign is separate: benchmarks/results/corrected/pause-state-{linux,mac}.json:2–32 records the same Git HEAD but different source hashes and full_corrected_campaign_started: false. Git HEAD alone does not identify the tested build.
  • platform-comparison.md:112–130 correctly retains the four original metallic-sphere failures, identifies the later Linux fix separately, and limits convergence conclusions.
  • Unverified scope: “Every result” at platform-comparison.md:8–9 extends the identity claim to macOS; the inspected Linux archive cannot establish that. Narrow the statement or supply the Mac manifests.
  • The original Linux manifests do record 2026-09-12 start times, so evidence.md:31 (“No file records the date”) is unnecessarily broad.

Missing corrected Mac qualification is a remaining evidence gap, not proof that the historical comparison’s results are false. Read-only inspection; no execution or edits.

Confirmed smallest coherent fix: use complex128 PARITY_CHANGE @ compact @ PARITY_CHANGE.T inside _layers, before selecting requested ports.

  • Mathematically identical to current pair-gather conversion and existing NumPy implementation.
  • Preserves partial/reordered ports and linear scaling with transverse groups.
  • Reduces eight traced array operations to two matmuls.
  • Keep resolve_poltype validation and all material/achirality guards.
  • Use b.array(PARITY_CHANGE, complex_=True) for Torch dtype compatibility.

Source verified; no edits, tests, or timing performed. Findings sent to root and correctness.
